$description: Raft Design System tokens in the Design Tokens Community Group format (2025.10). This file is the source of packages/ui/src/foundation.css: edit it, then run `vp run @botiverse/raft-ui#build:tokens`. Extensions under "build.botiverse.raft": `modes.dark` is the dark-mode value; `scope` is `root` for mode-independent palette values and `every-mode` for aliases declared again in each mode scope; `css: true` marks a value kept as a CSS expression (color-mix, multi-layer shadows) that the format has no type for.

on-hud-muted.$description: Secondary text on the HUD: the shortcut in a tooltip, the detail line of a toast.

veil.$description: The cover over something busy or loading in place: an image uploading or that failed, a preview being prepared. The page at 80%, so what is under it shows through, dimmed, and a default-colour Spinner on it reads in both modes. Translucent by contract, like the two backdrops.

subtle.$description: Hover tier subtle (light): hover on large things people read, a row, a message, a readable card, and a row whose menu is open. About 2.5 to 3 OKLab dE in both modes, on paper, the sidebar and cards alike, under every selection tint, so text keeps its contrast.

medium.$description: Hover tier medium: hover on small controls (buttons, icon buttons, chips, tabs, segment items) and press on everything, on paper-coloured surfaces. About 5.5 to 6.5 OKLab dE; dark is lighter than light because the same ink alpha shows more on a dark surface.

frame-medium.$description: Hover tier medium on the frame (rail items, on-frame buttons, the workspace button): hover and press. Its own alphas because ink shows differently on the yellow and on the near-black frame: 10% on the yellow and 6% on the dark frame land on the medium step, about 6 OKLab dE.

cell-hover.$description: A list cell's hover and its menu-open fill (lib/list-cell.ts), drawn on the cell's inset shape. fill-subtle in light. In dark it steps up to 7.5% ink, so the rounded shape reads on a dark surface, where fill-subtle's 3% barely shows. Rows only: the global tiers don't change.

cell-press.$description: A list cell's press fill, the same with a mouse and on a touch screen. fill-medium in light. In dark 12% ink, a clear step over the cell's dark hover.

cell-selected.$description: A list cell that is selected or open beside its list (an active InboxItem, a selected ListRow), and the located highlight on a cell. info-soft in light. In dark the cyan at 38% instead of 18%, so a selected cell stands out from a hovered one.

field.$description: The frame of a field and the composer: the ink and width of line-strong, drawn 1.5px.

hover.$description: Hovering or pressing a sticker lays sticker-medium (10% ink) over its colour.

you.$description: Raft yellow for what is addressed to you: a mention of you, the sidebar's @ marker, a search hit, the passage of the comment you opened. Its own value, not brand, so a theme that grays the brand (Boring Gray) keeps it yellow.

selected.$description: Raft yellow for the selected sticker: where you are (the active sidebar row, a segment, a tab, the tab bar's item, the current step) and what is on (a switch, a toggle, a pressed panel action). Its own value, not brand, so a theme that grays the brand (Boring Gray) keeps it yellow.

$root.$description: Every solid is a sticker: ink type on the colour in both modes.

graphic.$description: A failure or warning drawn as a graphic in data visualisation: the fill or stroke of a chart mark, such as a failed route in a migration chart. The warning orange, deep enough in light mode and bright in dark mode to stand at least 3:1 against the canvas, sidebar, card and popover (WCAG 1.4.11). Never text: warning text takes warning-strong.

$root.$description: danger = the destructive sticker (red fill, ink type); danger-strong is the error ink for invalid fields and destructive menu items.

float.$description: Controls never cast a shadow; only overlays float.

edge.$description: The fade at the edge of a strip that scrolls sideways (mask-fade-x): long enough to say more is there, short enough to leave the item under it readable.

content.$description: The fade where content is cut (mask-fade-t, mask-fade-b): a long message folded, a glimpse of hidden history. About two lines, so the cut reads as a fold, not a clipped line.

dimmed.$description: Something present but not active: deleted, offline or still pending (opacity-dimmed). The place a dragged item came from keeps its own 0.4 (data-drag-origin).

drag-settle-duration.$description: A drag settling: the lifted copy gliding into its place on a drop or back home on a cancel, siblings sliding apart to open the place, and a layout reflowing on a drop.

drag-settle-easing.$description: The ease-out of drag-settle-duration: fast off the hand, slow into place.

ring.$description: The focus indicator. It shows only after keyboard navigation: styles.css empties it while the root carries data-input-modality="pointer", which installInputModality sets after a click or a tap.

selection.$description: Selected text (::selection). brand-soft in light mode; in dark mode brand over the page at 22%, the wash of a commented passage, because brand-soft left a selection almost the same as the page.

gap.$description: Between two fields of a form, and between the parts of a form section: two airs.

height.$description: A default control: a field, a select, a Button, a tab, a selected segment, a menu option, a sidebar row. A finger's 44px on a phone; 34px on a desktop, the one desktop size for all of them (stdrc, 2026-11-04; Feishu's 32px before).

height-cta.$description: The full-width call to action across a sign-in, sign-up or setup form (Button xl).

icon-size.$description: The icon in a control-height icon button.

hit-inset.$description: How far a control-height button's hit area reaches past its top and bottom, to keep 44px.

embedded-inset.$description: How far a chip or a button embedded in a field, the composer or a corner sits inside its frame's outer edge, and from its sibling.

embedded-size.$description: A chip or a button embedded in a field: the control height less the embedded inset above and below, so the field keeps its height.

air.$description: The air of the size chain: between a label, its control and its help, around a control in a bar, and half of the gap between two fields. Every step below is the control height plus or minus a number of airs.

radius.$description: The corner of a control at the control height (a field, a Select, a Button at lg and icon-lg), about a quarter of its height: 10px at 44 on a phone and a touch screen, 8px at 34 on a desktop.

height.$description: Every header: a panel, a sidebar or a thread head, a dialog's bar, a drawer's head, a rail head. The control height with the header air above and below, so the seams of a screen line up.

air.$description: The air above and below the control in a header: one control air on a phone and a touch screen (44 + 12 = 56); 5px on a desktop, so a 34px control and its head make 44 (34 + 10).

height-short.$description: Every header in a window shorter than 600px. On a desktop, a bar button with one air above and below (28 + 12 = 40).

size.$description: An icon button in a bar: a head's actions and its x, the composer's icons, a row's actions. The control height on a phone and a touch screen; 28px on a desktop, the size of the header's icon tile, so a head's tile and buttons share one size and one centre line. Its hit area still reaches 44px.

radius.$description: The corner of a bar button, about a quarter of its height: 10px at 44 on a phone and a touch screen, 6px at the 28px bar button with a mouse on a desktop.

height.$description: An item on the frame: the top bar's and the title bar's buttons, the workspace button and the search box. 36px on a phone and a touch screen; the control height on a desktop, so the top bar is a header (34 + 2 x 5 = 44 with a mouse).

width.$description: The switch's track: 50 x 30 on a phone and a touch screen, macOS's regular 38 x 22 on a desktop. Its knob is the track height less 8px (a 1.5px border and 2.5px of padding each side, so the 1px of track between the knob's ring and the border stays) and travels the width less the height.

height.$description: A sidebar row from 768px, 2px apart; its highlight fills the row. On a desktop the control height (34px): one size for a sidebar item, a menu option, a compact list row, a field, a select, a Button, a tab and a selected segment (stdrc, 2026-11-04). A phone list of places keeps 44px.
An option of a popup list or a menu item with one line: 36px on a phone and a touch screen, the row height (34px, the control height) on a desktop.

inset.$description: Above and below the tallest part of a settings row (ListRow plain): two airs.

gap.$description: Between two sections of a form (FormSection), half above and half below the hairline between them: 32px on a phone and a touch screen, two field gaps (24px) on a desktop.

top.$description: From a head's seam to the first thing of the content under it: the page inset on a phone and a touch screen; 12px on a desktop, so the content sits close under its compact head (stdrc, 2026-11-05).

inset.$description: The inset of a column's content, a settings page, a drawer's body and a dialog's form: 16px on a phone and a touch screen; 16px with a mouse on a desktop too (20 before 2026-11-05), where the column margin, the list cells' content and the heads follow it, one edge.

width.$description: The rail, its 1px seam included: 57px on a touch screen, 49px on a desktop (48 + 1, the short window's rail). Its own size, not the header's.

item.$description: A rail item: 40px on a touch screen, 36px on a desktop.

width-short.$description: The rail in a window shorter than 600px, its 1px seam included; with a mouse the rail is always this width (48 + 1).

item-short.$description: A rail item in a window shorter than 600px; with a mouse rail items are always this size.

gap-message.$description: The message step of a timeline: from the last line of one turn to the first line of the next (a sender line, an event line). Every row keeps the row inset above and below its text; the first row of a turn adds the rest above it.

gap-section.$description: The section step of a timeline, one step wider than the message step: either side of a date line, from the top of the list to the first line, and from the last line to the composer, so a boundary reads as one and the last message never sits on the composer.

row-inset.$description: How far a timeline row's hover and selected highlight reaches above and below its text. Two rows of one turn sit two insets apart.

medium.$description: Hover tier medium on a colour sticker (primary, warning and danger buttons, colour badges, the selected segment on press): hover and press, 10% ink in both modes.

ink-medium.$description: Hover tier medium on an ink sticker (the server tile in the rail or the sidebar header): hover, press and open, 6% paper in both modes, since ink laid over ink doesn't show.

busy.$description: Yellow for an agent at work, and for Status variant="primary". The value of brand in Raft Yellow, but its own, so a theme that grays the brand (Boring Gray) keeps a working agent yellow.

busy-soft.$description: The tint of the Working chip (Badge variant="busy"). The value of brand-soft in Raft Yellow, but its own, so Boring Gray keeps it yellow.

read-mark.$description: The check after a mention once the agent mentioned has read the message (MessageReferenceReadMark). A bare check has no ink box around it, so it takes a lime dark enough to read on the page: palette-lime-700 in light mode (6.2:1 on white; the online lime is 1.64:1), the online lime in dark mode (10.5:1 on the dark canvas).
